case_name: Carl David Lucas and Jasmine Lucas v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Resided in Maryland when Petition filed (September 28, 2020). Separated in 2019; Ms. Lucas (California at the time) prepared and filed the joint 2018 return. Mr. Lucas an Army reservist; four employers between them (DC Government, Friends of Guest House, DFAS, Cybraics).

adjustments: unreported income (wages; Principal Life Form 1099-R distribution)
10% additional tax on early distribution from a qualified plan
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Unreported wages; itemized and reservist deductions claimed on Form 1040X; withholding credit; innocent spouse relief for Ms. Lucas; penalty
conceded: Petitioners conceded they received and failed to report income from Principal Life on Form 1099-R
Petitioners conceded they are liable for the 10% additional tax on the Principal Life income
Petitioners conceded they are not entitled to the American Opportunity Tax Credit
Petitioners deemed to have abandoned/conceded the $13,800 moving expense deduction
Respondent conceded petitioners entitled to child and dependent care credit, child tax credit and additional child tax credit
Respondent conceded deduction of state and local income taxes of $10,000
Respondent conceded deduction of home mortgage interest of $22,563
Respondent conceded a credit for excess Social Security taxes withheld of $1,110

findings_of_fact.fact: On the 2018 Form 1040 petitioners reported total income of $81,407: DFAS wages $76,445 and state tax refund $4,962
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioners reported total income of $81,407, consisting of wages of $76,445 from DFAS and a state tax refund received of $4,962.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioners stipulated they received wages of $206,609 and did not dispute the Forms W-2
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioners stipulated that they received wages of $206,609.
(1) petitioners received and failed to report wages of $174,995;

findings_of_fact.fact: Reported withholding $19,960; stipulated actual withholding $12,271; overreported $7,689
findings_of_fact.snippet: The parties stipulated that petitioners had $12,271 of income tax withheld for 2018 and therefore overreported $7,689 of tax withheld.

findings_of_fact.fact: Medical expense deduction of $35,310 claimed on Form 1040X; no substantiating documents provided even with record held open until January 3, 2024
findings_of_fact.snippet: On the amended return petitioners claimed itemized deductions for medical expenses of $35,310 and noncash charitable contributions of $85,000

findings_of_fact.fact: Noncash charitable deductions: $50,000 to Goodwill (November 2, 2018) and $35,000 to Friends of Guest House (December 1, 2018); receipts lacked adequate description/date
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioners claimed noncash charitable contribution deductions for a $50,000 donation to Goodwill on November 2, 2018,

findings_of_fact.fact: Reservist expenses claimed $29,445; stipulated $2,433 nonmeal unreimbursed travel over 4,464 total miles (12 round trips of 372 miles Maryland to New Jersey); remaining $27,012 unsupported
findings_of_fact.snippet: the parties stipulated that Mr. Lucas incurred $2,433 in nonmeal, unreimbursed travel expenses.

findings_of_fact.fact: Ms. Lucas prepared the return omitting her own wages from two employers and Mr. Lucas's Cybraics wages despite having his W-2s; court finds actual knowledge
findings_of_fact.snippet: we find that Ms. Lucas had actual knowledge that the 2018 Form 1040 did not include all income

findings_of_fact.fact: Penalty received timely managerial approval; no evidence of reasonable cause
findings_of_fact.snippet: The penalty received timely managerial approval.

issues.question: Did petitioners receive and fail to report wages of $174,995 for 2018?
issues.holding: Yes; petitioners stipulated receipt of $206,609 of wages and did not dispute the Forms W-2; unreported income determination sustained
issues.computable_reason: Stipulated wages received vs. wages reported; inclusion under §61(a)(1) is mechanical

issues.question: Other (withholding credit / jurisdiction): Can the Court redetermine petitioners' claimed excess federal tax withholdings of $7,689?
issues.holding: No; a deficiency is determined without regard to the §31 credit, so the Court lacks jurisdiction to redetermine the withholding-credit adjustment
issues.computable_reason: Pure legal rule under §6211(b)(1): withholding credits excluded from deficiency

issues.question: Other (medical expense deduction §213): Are petitioners entitled to deduct $35,310 of medical expenses?
Other (noncash charitable contributions §170): Are petitioners entitled to deduct $85,000 of noncash charitable contributions?
issues.holding: No; receipts lacked date and/or reasonably sufficient description; testimony uncorroborated

issues.question: Other (Armed Forces reservist travel §62(a)(2)(E)/§162(p)): Are petitioners entitled to deduct $29,445 of reservist expenses?
issues.holding: Allowed $2,433 as stipulated; remaining $27,012 disallowed for lack of evidence
issues.computable_reason: Allowed amount rests on stipulation; remainder disallowed for lack of substantiation

issues.question: Other (innocent spouse §6015(b)): Is Ms. Lucas entitled to relief from joint and several liability under section 6015(b)?
issues.holding: No; she had actual knowledge of the omitted income, failing §6015(b)(1)(C); Court not bound by stipulation not signed by Mr. Lucas
issues.computable_reason: Knowledge finding is a factual/evidentiary determination

issues.question: Are petitioners liable for the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty for a substantial understatement for 2018?
issues.holding: Liable to the extent the understatement exceeds the greater of 10% of tax required to be shown or $5,000, to be determined in the Rule 155 computation; approval obtained and no reasonable cause shown
issues.computable_reason: Remaining question is the 10%/$5,000 substantial-understatement threshold after recomputation; approval and no reasonable cause found

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Unreported wages sustained; no jurisdiction over withholding credit; medical and charitable deductions disallowed; reservist expenses allowed only $2,433; innocent spouse relief denied; 6662(a) penalty applies if understatement substantial after Rule 155 computation

notes: Opinion rounds amounts to nearest dollar. Stipulation of Settled Issues between respondent and Ms. Lucas not binding because Mr. Lucas did not sign (Rule 91(e)). Derived: $206,609 - $76,445 = $130,164 (does not equal $174,995; the $174,995 figure is as framed by the court, possibly including other items); modeller should rely on stated figures. Form 1040X was not processed by respondent.
